name: orb_wide_range_fade_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when the 09:15-09:30 opening range exceeds 2x its 20-session average, institutional option writers at the ORB extreme strikes (puts at ORB_low, calls at ORB_high) become heavily gamma-exposed and delta-hedge aggressively against further extension. Simultaneously, VWAP-benchmarked buy-side desks — seeing the index pinned at the ORB extreme — begin fading the deviation to protect their intraday benchmark. Each subsequent test of the ORB extreme generates a 10-20 spot point micro-rejection within 30-90 seconds as these two flows converge. At 5-second resolution we enter the instant RSI exhaustion confirms the rejection is beginning, capturing the first leg of the mean-reversion toward ORB midpoint before the move extends.

indicators.name: orb_high_15
indicators.formula: max(high) for bars where time_minutes in [555, 570)
indicators.purpose: Opening range high (09:15-09:30 = 15 min = 180 bars). FIXED TIME WINDOW — not scaled by frequency. The same 15-minute window regardless of bar size defines where institutional supply was established at the open.

indicators.name: orb_low_15
indicators.formula: min(low) for bars where time_minutes in [555, 570)
indicators.purpose: Opening range low (09:15-09:30). FIXED TIME WINDOW. Paired with orb_high_15 to define the opening auction boundaries.

indicators.name: avg_orb_range_20d
indicators.purpose: 20-session rolling average ORB range. NOT scaled — this is a cross-session normalizer. 20 sessions ≈ 1 month of trading days, enough to establish a stable baseline range for NIFTY's typical opening volatility without being stale. The original also used 20 sessions.

indicators.name: price_position
indicators.purpose: Normalized price within the ORB range (0=at low, 1=at high). Identifies when NIFTY is approaching either ORB extreme. Entry zone: price_position > 0.85 (near high) or < 0.15 (near low).

indicators.name: rsi_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute RSI (36 bars × 5s) for micro-exhaustion detection at ORB extremes. Original used RSI(14) at 1-min = 14-minute window. We compress to 3 minutes because we are catching the INTRABAR exhaustion signal at the ORB extreme touch, not confirming a completed session-level reversal. A 3-min RSI above 70 at the ORB high means the micro-rally into the high is overbought — the fading thesis is active.

conditions: price_position > 0.85 (close within top 15% of ORB range)
vix_close < 22 (extreme VIX days may extend rather than revert)
buy_pe.confirmation: RSI turning down from above 70 confirms the micro-rejection is starting

conditions: price_position < 0.15 (close within bottom 15% of ORB range)
vix_close < 22 (extreme VIX days may extend rather than revert)
buy_ce.confirmation: RSI turning up from below 30 confirms the micro-bounce is starting

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option pts = ~8 spot pts extension beyond the ORB extreme. On NIFTY, if the index extends >8 spot pts beyond the ORB extreme after the RSI exhaustion signal, the fading thesis has failed and momentum is breaking out rather than reverting. At delta ~0.5, 4 option pts = 8 spot pts, which is the threshold between normal noise and genuine ORB extension.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option pts = ~14 spot pts reversion toward ORB midpoint. Micro-rejections at NIFTY ORB extremes on wide-range days typically yield 10-20 spot pt bounces within 60-90 seconds before the next pause. 7 pts captures ~50-70% of the expected 10-20 spot pt first leg (1:1.75 R:R). Consistent with NIFTY 1-min typical move of 3-7 option pts at ATM delta.

filters.vix_filter: vix_close < 22.0 — on NIFTY, VIX > 22 signals regime where wide ORB ranges continue expanding rather than reverting (panic/trend days)
filters.time_filter: 09:35-15:25 IST — enter only after ORB has fully formed (09:30); allow until 15:25 since ORB extremes remain relevant all day on wide-range sessions
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume is institutional and noisy at 5s; the ORB range width itself is the volume proxy
filters.trend_filter: none applied explicitly — the wide_range filter and VIX filter together exclude strong trend days where ORB fade fails
filters.spread_filter: not applicable — limit orders at candle close, no bid-ask cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — if NIFTY ORB patterns become widely known and faded by algos, the micro-rejection signals may be front-run and weakened

adaptation_notes: Original: fade NIFTY50 stocks when 15-min ORB > 2x avg, hold 20-120 min, target ORB midpoint. Converted: same trigger (wide ORB day, price at extreme, RSI exhaustion) but targets the MICRO-REJECTION at each ORB extreme test (15-120 second hold) rather than the full-session mean reversion. This is valid because: (1) the ORB is a FIXED TIME WINDOW — same 15 minutes regardless of bar size; (2) the RSI was compressed from 14-min to 3-min to detect intrabar exhaustion rather than session-level reversal; (3) the target changes from 'reach ORB midpoint' (may take hours) to 'capture first 10-20 spot pt micro-rejection leg' (completes in 30-90 seconds). The VIX < 22 filter replaces the original's 'NIFTY not in extreme trend > 2%' filter with a more quantifiable index-level regime check. The equity-specific event_filter (skip news-driven wide ranges) is dropped — NIFTY index cannot have stock-specific news, and macro events that widen the ORB still create valid ORB extreme S/R zones.
weaknesses: Wide ORB days on NIFTY are infrequent (10-15% of sessions), producing low signal density — the strategy must be combined with others
On RBI/FOMC announcement days, wide ORB ranges may extend continuously rather than revert — the VIX filter partially mitigates but doesn't eliminate this risk
The 20-session lookback for avg_orb_range requires sufficient cross-session data; in backtests with short windows the baseline may be unreliable
